findings.title: Verifier compares sanitizer-canonicalized HTML to raw text, flagging valid markup
findings.body:
verifySafeHtml() compares the OWASP sanitizer output with the original translation using Objects.equals (line 99). The sanitizer re-serializes allowed markup in its own canonical form (it renders `
`/`
` as `
`), so a translation using an equivalent but differently written tag is reported as "Illegal HTML" even though it is valid and permitted by POLICY_SOME_HTML. This already forced the PR to rewrite the `webauthn-error-*` lines in ~15 locale files from `
` to `
` for no functional reason, and the next translator who writes `
` (or `
`) will get a failing build with a misleading message. Both sides should be normalized (e.g. compare sanitized forms of value and expected value, or normalize `` before reporting).

findings.title: Anchor mismatch message does not say which key/file failed
findings.body: When a translation's anchor tag does not exactly match the English source, the verifier adds "Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string" to the messages list. Unlike the Illegal HTML message, it contains neither the message key nor the file. Because the verifier runs over every locale of every theme, a failing build cannot tell the developer which entry to fix, and the same entry typically also produces a generic "Illegal HTML" message. Include key and file, as the Illegal HTML message does.

findings.title: Lithuanian account totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The new value of `totpStep1` is `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The old Lithuanian sentence was replaced with a string copied from another locale while fixing the stale <a> links, so Lithuanian users of the account console will now see Italian text on the OTP setup page. It needs a real Lithuanian translation (e.g. of "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:").

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: `loginTotpStep1` was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` (Italian) in the Lithuanian login bundle. The removed value was Lithuanian; this replacement is a copy/paste from the Italian locale, so Lithuanian users see Italian instructions during OTP/TOTP setup. It must be translated to Lithuanian.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese bundle receives Traditional Chinese text
findings.body: The new `totpStep1` value `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式) in the zh_CN (Simplified) file; the rest of this file uses Simplified forms (e.g. `mobile=手机`). The text appears to have been copied from a zh_TW translation and needs to be converted to Simplified Chinese (手机/应用程序).

findings.title: Frontend message changed from {{n}} interpolation to Java MessageFormat choice syntax
findings.body: Every other entry in this account-ui bundle uses the frontend i18n placeholder style `{{0}}`/`{{1}}` (e.g. `error-invalid-length='{{0}}' must have a length between {{1}} and {{2}}.`), but `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} ... {{1}} ... {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} ... {1} ... {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` — single-brace Java MessageFormat syntax plus a ChoiceFormat sub-message. If this key is rendered by the same i18n mechanism as its neighbours, the `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` placeholders will not be substituted and users will see the raw `{2,choice,...}` expression. The same change was made to `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties` line 3139 (which also previously used `{{0}}`).

findings.title: No positive-case tests for the new HTML verification
findings.body:
All added tests only assert that problems are detected (illegal tag, HTML in a no-HTML message, changed anchor). There is no test asserting that a valid file produces an empty messages list, i.e. that a translation using the same anchors as the English source, an allowed `
`, and the special-cased keys (`error-invalid-multivalued-size`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`) passes cleanly. A regression that makes the sanitizer reject every legitimate translation (as the `
` serialization issue already shows is easy) would not be caught by unit tests, only by a repository-wide build.
